title: Missile strike hits Freedom Square and regional administration in Kharkiv
body:
On 1 March 2022 Russian strikes hit central Freedom Square in Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, and damaged the Kharkiv Regional State Administration building. A residential building on Novo-Bavarian Avenue was also hit. Oleg Synegubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, called the strikes a war crime.

According to preliminary figures from Synegubov reported by Ukrainska Pravda, seven people were killed and 24 injured at the square, including one child. At least eight dead were earlier reported at the Novo-Bavarian Avenue building, which was completely destroyed. Many people were believed to be trapped under the debris, and the toll was still being clarified.

Ukrainian officials said that the square was struck by a Russian missile. Ukrainska Pravda also reported that Ukrainian defenders had shot down a Russian bomb carrier that had destroyed an apartment building that day. Kharkiv had been under bombardment since the start of the full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022, and its fighting formed part of the eastern front of the Russian offensive.
